title: Numbers, age & quantities
goal: Count things, ask and give ages, ask 'how many / how much', and use ordinal numbers from first to tenth.
intro:
Look at the **numbers chart** for 0–100 first: Pashto numbers are fairly regular. From 21 to 99 you say the unit and then the ten (like old English 'four-and-twenty'): پنځه ويشت = 'five twenty' = 25. Only 11–19 and a few forms in the twenties need special care.

In Pakistan you'll also hear large numbers counted in **لک** (lak, 100,000) and **کروړ** (kroṛ, 10 million); in Afghanistan people more often say سل زره (100 thousand) and مليون. In this unit you'll use numbers with nouns, ask about age and quantity, and learn first, second, third…

grammar.title: Counting nouns
grammar.body:
**One** has two forms: **يو** yaw with masculine nouns and **يوه** yáwa with feminine ones: يو هلک 'a boy', يوه نجلۍ 'a girl'. يو/يوه also serves as 'a, an'.

After **two and higher** the noun goes into the **plural**: دوه سړي, درې ښځې, څلور ماشومان. Masculine nouns ending in a consonant often take a short **counting plural in -a** instead of the full plural: دوه **کاله** 'two years' (not کالونه), درې **کتابه** 'three books' (colloquial; the standard written plural is کتابونه). Units of measure usually don't change: پنځه کيلو، لس روپۍ.

Numbers come before the noun and mostly don't change for case, except that يو/يوه inflect like adjectives (oblique m. يوه, f. يوې) and دوه, درې have oblique forms دوو (dwo), درېيو (dreyo) after prepositions.

grammar.title: How many, how much, how old — and ordinals
grammar.body:
**څو** (tso) asks 'how many' about things you can count: څو ورځې؟ 'how many days?'. **څومره** (tsómra) asks 'how much': څومره اوبه؟ 'how much water?' — and also 'how much does it cost?' (unit 12).

For age, put **کلن** (kálan) 'years old' after the number; it agrees in gender: زه دېرش کلن يم (man) / زه دېرش کلنه يم (woman). You can also say زما عمر دېرش کاله دی 'my age is thirty years'.

**Ordinals** add **-əm** to the number: پنځم 'fifth', لسم 'tenth', شلم 'twentieth'. The first three are special: لومړی، دويم، درېيم. Ordinals are adjectives and agree with feminine nouns: لومړۍ ورځ 'the first day', دويمه خبره 'the second point'.

examples.native: څو کاله دې په کابل کې تېر کړي؟
examples.roman: tso kā́la de pə kābúl ke ter kə́ṛi?
examples.en: How many years have you spent in Kabul?

dialogue.title: Eid visit
dialogue.setting: On Eid, Aunt Malalai visits and talks to her neighbour's children, Wali and Mena.

lines.speaker: Wali
lines.native: زه نهه کلن يم، ترور جانې.
lines.roman: zə nə́hə kálan yəm, tror jā́ne.

lines.speaker: Malalai
lines.native: ماشاالله! او ته، لورې؟ ته څو کلنه يې؟
lines.roman: māshāllā́h! aw tə, lúre? tə tso kalána ye?
lines.en: Wonderful! And you, dear girl? How old are you?

lines.speaker: Mena
lines.native: زه شپږ کلنه يم. زه په لومړي ټولګي کې يم.
lines.roman: zə shpaẓ kalána yəm. zə pə lumṛí ṭolgí ke yəm.
lines.en: I'm six. I'm in first grade.

lines.speaker: Malalai
lines.native: دا واخلئ، دا ستاسو عيدي ده. هر يو ته لس روپۍ.
lines.roman: dā wā́xləy, dā stāso ʿidí da. har yaw ta las rupə́y.
lines.en: Here, take this — it's your Eid money. Ten rupees for each of you.

lines.speaker: Mena
lines.native: ډېره مننه! موږ دواړه ډېر خوشاله يو.
lines.roman: ḍéra manə́na! muẓ dwā́ṛa ḍer xoshā́la yu.
lines.en: Thank you so much! We're both very happy.

culture: On Eid (in Pashto **اختر** axtár — the 'small Eid' after Ramadan, کوچنی اختر, and the 'big Eid' of sacrifice, لوی اختر), children go from house to house in new clothes and receive **عيدي** — small gifts of money from relatives and neighbours. Adults greet each other with اختر مو مبارک شه 'may your Eid be blessed'. Ages are not always kept precisely in rural areas, and older people may give their age as a round number; it's polite not to press. Elders are asked their age rarely — asking a woman's age is best avoided altogether.

tip.title: One, two, three …
tip.body:
- 'One' agrees: **يو** with masculine nouns, **يوه** with feminine ones: يو هلک، يوه نجلۍ. It also means 'a, an'.
- From two up, the noun goes **plural**: دوه هلکان، درې لوڼې.
- Kilos and rupees don't change: پنځه کيلو، لس روپۍ.
tip.pattern: يو زوی  ·  يوه لور  ·  دوه لوڼې

tip.title: Age with کلن
tip.body:
- Number + **کلن** 'years old' + the verb: زه شل کلن يم.
- کلن agrees: **کلن** for a man or boy, **کلنه** for a woman or girl.
- Ask with **څو**: ته څو کلن يې؟ Politely: ستاسو عمر څومره دی؟ ('how much is your age?') — answer with **کاله** 'years': شل کاله.

sentences.native: زما د ورور عمر شل کاله دی.
sentences.roman: zmā də wror ʿumr shəl kā́la day.
sentences.en: My brother is twenty. (lit. my brother's age is twenty years)

sentences.native: انا مې نوي کلنه ده، ماشاالله.
sentences.roman: anā́ me nawí kalána da, māshāllā́h.
sentences.en: My grandmother is ninety, bless her.

tip.title: څو or څومره?
tip.body:
- **څو** 'how many' is for things you can count: څو مڼې؟
- **څومره** 'how much' is for amounts: څومره اوبه؟ څومره چای؟
- **نيم** 'half' goes first: نيم کيلو; يو نيم 'one and a half'.

sentences.en: How much English does your brother speak?
How many apples do you want?
Give me one and a half kilos of apples.
How many kilos of apples would you like?
How much Pashto do you understand?
How much tea do you drink?

lessons.title: First, second, third

tip.title: First, second, third …
tip.body:
- Most ordinals add **-əm** to the number: څلور → څلور**م**, پنځه → پنځ**م**, لس → لس**م**.
- The first three are special: **لومړی، دويم، درېيم**.
- They agree with feminine nouns: لومړ**ۍ** ورځ, دويم**ه** ورځ.
